easy.def: The tools and clothes you need for something.
examples: I packed my camping gear.
Put on your gear.
She has all her swim gear.

more.def: The equipment and clothes you need for an activity.
examples: We packed our camping gear in the car.
The hockey players put on their gear.
He carried his fishing gear to the lake.

easy.def: A wheel with bumps that turns another wheel.
examples: The gears turn the wheel.
The clock has small gears.
A bike has gears.

more.def: A wheel with teeth around the edge that fits into other wheels to make machines work.
examples: The gears inside the clock turn together.
A bike has gears that make it easier to go uphill.
The small gear turns the big one.

easy.def: The part of a car with gears.
examples: The gearbox is under the car.
A gearbox has gears.
The gearbox broke.

more.def: The part of an engine or vehicle that contains the gears.
examples: The mechanic fixed the gearbox.
A gearbox changes the speed of the wheels.
The car's gearbox made a grinding noise.

easy.def: A stick in a car that changes gears.
examples: Dad moved the gearshift.
The gearshift is a stick.
Push the gearshift.

more.def: A lever that the driver uses to change gears in a vehicle.
examples: Dad moved the gearshift into reverse.
The gearshift is between the front seats.
She learned to use the gearshift.

easy.def: A small lizard that can climb walls.
examples: A gecko climbed the wall.
The gecko is small.
We saw a gecko.

more.def: A small lizard with sticky feet that can climb walls and ceilings.
examples: A gecko clung to the ceiling of the porch.
The gecko's sticky feet grip smooth glass.
Geckos live in warm places.

easy.def: A thick, soft, jelly-like stuff.
examples: I put gel on my hair.
The gel is cool.
Aloe gel soothes the skin.

more.def: A thick, soft, jelly-like substance, such as the kind put in hair or in a cold pack.
examples: He combed a little gel into his hair.
The cold pack was filled with a blue gel.
Aloe gel helped soothe my sunburn.

easy.def: A food that makes things wobble when it sets.
examples: The dessert has gelatin.
Gelatin is jiggly.
I ate gelatin.

more.def: A clear, tasteless substance used to make jelly desserts set.
examples: The fruit dessert was set with gelatin.
Gelatin makes the jelly wobble.
We stirred gelatin into the warm liquid.

easy.def: A valuable stone that is cut and shiny.
examples: The ring has a gem.
The gem is red.
A gem sparkles.

more.def: A valuable stone that has been cut and polished, used in jewelry.
examples: The ring has a sparkling red gem.
The gem was cut into a diamond shape.
We saw many gems in the museum.

easy.def: Something or someone that is very special.
examples: He is a gem.
The book is a gem.
This is a hidden gem.

more.def: A person or thing that is special and much loved.
examples: He is a real gem and always helps.
The little cafe is a hidden gem.
This book is a gem that everyone should read.

easy.def: A jewel or precious stone.
examples: The gemstone sparkled.
A red gemstone.
She found a gemstone.

more.def: A valuable stone, often cut and polished, used in jewelry.
examples: The ring held a bright blue gemstone.
Rubies and emeralds are gemstones.
The crown was set with gemstones.

easy.def: Being a boy, a girl or neither.
examples: The form asks for your gender.
Games are for every gender.
Gender is part of who you are.

more.def: The way a person is described or thinks of themselves, such as a boy, a girl or neither.
examples: Clubs at our school are open to every gender.
The form asked for her name, age and gender.
In some languages, every noun has a gender.

easy.def: A tiny part of a living thing that tells it how to grow.
examples: You get genes from your parents.
Genes can make eyes brown.
A gene is tiny.

more.def: A tiny part inside the cells of a living thing that carries information about what it will look like and how it will grow.
examples: Genes decide whether a flower will be red or white.
You get your genes from your mother and father.
A gene in a plant can make it grow tall or short.

easy.def: Not exact; true for most things.
examples: The general rule is no running.
I have a general idea.
He gave a general answer.

more.def: Including or true for most people or things, and not exact.
examples: She gave us a general idea of how the game works.
The general rule is to put away your toys.
There was a general feeling of excitement.

easy.def: A very high leader in the army.
examples: The general led his soldiers.
The general gave an order.
A general sat at the table.

more.def: A very high officer in the army.
examples: The general planned the march across the mountains.
Soldiers saluted the general.
The general met with leaders from other countries.

easy.def: Usually.
examples: I generally eat at six.
Dogs are generally friendly.
It is generally warm in May.

more.def: In most cases, or most of the time.
examples: I generally eat dinner at six.
The weather here is generally mild in spring.
It is generally warm here in May.

easy.def: To make or produce something.
examples: The sun generates heat.
Windmills generate power.
The machine generated sparks.

more.def: To make or produce something, especially power or heat.
examples: Windmills generate power from the wind.
The big engine generates a lot of heat.
A good story can generate laughter in a room.

easy.def: All the people who are about the same age.
examples: My grandparents are an older generation.
The younger generation.
Three generations live in this house.

more.def: All the people born and living around the same time, or the time between a parent and child.
examples: Three generations of our family live in this house.
My grandfather's generation grew up without computers.
Each new generation learns from the last.

easy.def: Not a special brand name.
examples: A generic medicine.
Generic cereal.
A generic box.

more.def: Not having a special brand name, or general and not specific.
examples: Mom bought the generic cereal, which is cheaper than the brand name.
The generic medicine works just as well.
The card had a generic message that fit anyone.

easy.def: Being happy to give and share.
examples: Her generosity was kind.
We thanked him for his generosity.
Generosity makes friends.

more.def: The quality of being kind and ready to give and share.
examples: Her generosity warmed our hearts.
We thanked him for his generosity in sharing his lunch.
Their generosity helped the whole town.

easy.def: Happy to share and give.
examples: It was generous of you to share your snack.
The generous girl gave me half her snack.
My aunt is generous with hugs.

more.def: Willing to give time, money, or help to others freely.
examples: Our generous neighbor gave vegetables from her garden to everyone on the street.
He was generous with his time and helped every student.
A generous gift helped the town build a new playground.

easy.def: In a kind way that gives a lot.
examples: She generously shared.
He gave generously.
They generously helped.

more.def: In a way that gives more than is needed or expected.
examples: She generously shared her lunch with the new girl.
He tipped the waiter generously.
The neighbors generously gave us a whole basket of apples.

easy.def: A small cat-like animal with a spotted coat.
examples: A genet is a small animal.
The genet has spots.
I saw a genet.

more.def: A small, slender animal of Africa and Europe with a spotted coat and long tail.
examples: A genet crept through the trees.
The genet has spots and a ringed tail.
Genets hunt at night.

easy.def: Having to do with the traits passed from parents to children.
examples: Eye color is genetic.
The trait is genetic.
A genetic code.

more.def: Having to do with genes, the parts of cells that pass traits from parents to children.
examples: Eye color is a genetic trait.
The scientist studied genetic differences.
Curly hair can be genetic.

easy.def: The study of how traits pass from parents to children.
examples: Genetics is about traits.
Genetics explains eye color.
She studies genetics.

more.def: The study of how features such as eye color are passed from parents to their children.
examples: Genetics explains why you have your mom's eyes.
She studies genetics at college.
Genetics shows how traits are passed down.

easy.def: Friendly and kind.
examples: The genial man smiled.
A genial host.
The genial baker.

more.def: Friendly, cheerful and kind.
examples: The genial host welcomed us in.
The baker was a genial man.
Her genial smile put us at ease.

easy.def: A magic spirit in stories that gives wishes.
examples: The genie gave me three wishes.
A genie is in the lamp.
The genie is magic.

more.def: A magic spirit in old stories that lives in a lamp or bottle and gives wishes to the person who frees it.
examples: The genie gave him three wishes.
In the story, a genie lived inside a golden lamp.
The genie floated out of the bottle in a puff of blue smoke.

easy.def: A person who is very, very smart.
examples: He is a genius.
The genius solved the puzzle.
A genius made it.

more.def: A person who has an unusually high ability to think or create.
examples: The young girl was a math genius.
The scientist was a genius.
The musician was a genius who wrote songs at age five.

easy.def: A kind of book, movie or music.
examples: Mystery is a genre.
What genre do you like?
Fantasy is a genre.

more.def: A type or kind of book, film or music, such as mystery or fantasy.
examples: Mystery is my favorite genre.
The library sorts books by genre.
Rock is a genre of music.

easy.def: Polite and proper.
examples: A genteel lady.
The genteel manner.
A genteel tea party.

more.def: Polite, refined and well-mannered, sometimes in a fussy way.
examples: The genteel lady sipped her tea.
They held a genteel tea party.
He spoke in a genteel way.

easy.def: Soft and kind, not rough.
examples: Be gentle with the baby.
The gentle horse let me pet it.
Use a gentle voice in the library.

more.def: Kind, calm, and careful; not rough or strong.
examples: A gentle rain fell on the garden all morning.
The nurse was gentle when she cleaned the cut.
A gentle breeze moved the leaves.

easy.def: A man who is polite and kind.
examples: The gentleman held the door for us.
Grandpa is a true gentleman.
Two gentlemen sat on a bench.

more.def: A man who is polite and well-behaved, or any man when you are speaking politely.
examples: The old gentleman tipped his hat to everyone he met.
Ladies and gentlemen, please take your seats because the show is starting.
A gentleman always lets others go first through the door.

easy.def: In a soft, kind way.
examples: Pet the cat gently.
She patted the baby gently.
He held the bird gently.

more.def: In a soft and careful way that does not hurt.
examples: Pet the puppy gently.
The nurse gently wrapped the bandage.
A gentle breeze moved the leaves.

easy.def: Real, not fake.
examples: The gold is genuine.
He has a genuine smile.
The coin is genuine.

more.def: Real and true, not pretend.
examples: The coin is made of genuine gold.
She gave me a genuine smile.
The painting turned out to be genuine.

easy.def: Truly.
examples: She is genuinely kind.
I am genuinely sorry.
He was genuinely happy.

more.def: In a way that is honest and real, not pretend.
examples: She was genuinely happy to see her grandmother.
I am genuinely sorry that I broke your toy.
He genuinely loves to read about space.

easy.def: A group of living things that are closely related.
examples: Lions are in the same genus as tigers.
A genus has many kinds.
The genus has three kinds.

more.def: A group of closely related plants or animals, larger than a species.
examples: Lions and tigers belong to the same genus.
A genus can include many different species.
Scientists put the new plant in the right genus.

easy.def: A rock that is hollow and filled with crystals.
examples: A geode has crystals.
Crack the geode.
The geode sparkled.

more.def: A rock that is hollow inside and lined with sparkling crystals.
examples: She cracked open the geode.
The geode was filled with purple crystals.
A geode looks plain outside and sparkles inside.

easy.def: Made of many triangles that form a dome.
examples: A geodesic dome.
The dome is geodesic.
We saw a geodesic dome.

more.def: Describing a round building or structure made of many connected triangles.
examples: The playground had a geodesic dome.
A geodesic dome is built from triangles.
The greenhouse was a geodesic structure.

easy.def: A person who studies maps and the Earth.
examples: The geographer drew a map.
A geographer studies land.
She is a geographer.

more.def: A person who studies the Earth's land, seas, climate and people.
examples: The geographer studied the mountains and rivers.
A geographer makes maps.
The geographer traveled to the desert.

easy.def: About places and maps.
examples: We looked at a geographic map.
The geographic facts are here.
A geographic book showed rivers.

more.def: Having to do with geography, which is the study of the earth and its places.
examples: The map shows geographic features such as rivers and mountains.
We learned about the geographic location of each country.
The geographic area around the lake is flat.

easy.def: Having to do with places and land.
examples: A geographical map.
The geographical facts.
A geographical feature.

more.def: Having to do with geography, which is the study of places and the Earth.
examples: We studied the geographical features of the country.
The geographical map showed rivers and mountains.
A river is a geographical feature.

easy.def: The study of the Earth, its land, seas and countries.
examples: We study geography.
Geography is about maps.
I like geography.

more.def: The study of the Earth, including its mountains, rivers, oceans, countries and the people who live there.
examples: In geography class we learned about the mountains and rivers of Asia.
She loves geography and can name every country on the map.
The geography of the island includes a tall mountain and a long beach.

easy.def: About rocks and the earth.
examples: A geological map.
The geological find.
We saw a geological site.

more.def: Having to do with geology, which is the study of rocks and the Earth.
examples: The class studied a geological map of the area.
A geological survey found gold.
The canyon is a famous geological site.

easy.def: A scientist who studies rocks and the earth.
examples: The geologist looked at a rock.
A geologist studies mountains.
The geologist found a fossil.

more.def: A scientist who studies rocks, soil and how the Earth is made.
examples: The geologist hiked up the mountain to collect rocks.
A geologist can tell how old a rock is.
The geologist explained how canyons are cut by rivers.

easy.def: The study of rocks and the earth.
examples: Geology is about rocks.
I like geology.
She studies geology.

more.def: The science of the Earth, its rocks and how they change over time.
examples: Geology tells how mountains were made.
She studies geology and collects rocks.
We learned about volcanoes in geology.

easy.def: Made of shapes like circles and squares.
examples: A geometric pattern.
The geometric design.
The rug is geometric.

more.def: Having to do with shapes and lines, or made of them.
examples: The rug had a geometric pattern of squares and triangles.
She drew a geometric design.
The tiles formed a geometric shape.

easy.def: The part of math about shapes and sizes.
examples: We learned geometry.
Geometry has triangles.
I like geometry.

more.def: The part of math that deals with shapes, lines, angles and sizes.
examples: In geometry, we learned about triangles and circles.
Geometry helps builders plan houses.
She solved the geometry problem by drawing a diagram.

easy.def: A garden flower with round leaves and bright blooms.
examples: The geranium is red.
Geraniums grow in pots.
A geranium bloomed.

more.def: A plant with round leaves and bright clusters of pink, red or white flowers, often grown in pots.
examples: Red geraniums bloomed in the window box.
Geraniums are easy to grow in pots.
A geranium sat on the porch.

easy.def: A small furry pet with long back legs.
examples: I have a gerbil.
The gerbil runs fast.
A gerbil is small.

more.def: A small, furry animal with long back legs that is often kept as a pet.
examples: My gerbil likes to run on its wheel.
The gerbil stuffed seeds in its cheeks.
Gerbils dig tunnels in wood shavings.

easy.def: A tiny living thing that can make you sick.
examples: Washing your hands gets rid of germs.
A germ is very small.
Germs can make you sick.

more.def: A tiny living thing that can cause illness.
examples: Sneezing into your elbow stops germs from spreading.
A germ is too small to see without a microscope.
Germs spread when people cough without covering their mouths.

easy.def: To start to grow from a seed.
examples: The seed germinated.
Beans germinate quickly.
Seeds germinate in the spring.

more.def: To begin to grow, as a seed does.
examples: The bean seed germinated in three days.
Seeds germinate when it is warm and wet.
The sunflower seeds germinated in the soil.

easy.def: When a seed starts to grow.
examples: Germination is sprouting.
The seed began germination.
Germination takes water.

more.def: The time when a seed begins to sprout and grow into a plant.
examples: Germination begins when the seed gets water.
Bean germination takes a few days.
Warm soil helps the seed's germination.

easy.def: Tiny things that can make you sick.
examples: Soap washes away germs.
Germs are too small to see.
Cover your mouth to stop germs.

more.def: Tiny living things, too small to see, that can cause sickness when they get inside the body.
examples: Washing your hands with soap gets rid of germs.
Germs can spread when someone sneezes without covering their nose.
A microscope shows germs that your eyes cannot see.

easy.def: Full of germs.
examples: The doorknob is germy.
A germy toy.
The germy sink.

more.def: Covered with germs.
examples: Wash your hands after touching germy doorknobs.
The germy toy needs cleaning.
The germy cup went into the sink.

easy.def: A verb with -ing that works like a noun.
examples: Running is a gerund.
A gerund ends in -ing.
Find the gerund.

more.def: A word ending in -ing that is made from a verb and is used as a noun.
examples: In "Swimming is fun," swimming is a gerund.
A gerund ends in -ing.
Find the gerund in this sentence.

easy.def: To use your hands a lot while talking.
examples: He gesticulated wildly.
She gesticulates as she talks.
They gesticulated.

more.def: To make lively movements with your arms and hands while speaking.
examples: He gesticulated wildly as he told the story.
She gesticulates when she is excited.
The coach gesticulated to show the plan.

easy.def: A hand movement that means something.
examples: A wave is a gesture.
He made a gesture.
The gesture meant stop.

more.def: A movement of your hands or body that shows a meaning or feeling.
examples: A wave is a friendly gesture.
He made a gesture for us to be quiet.
A thumbs-up gesture means good job.

easy.def: To have something come to you or to go and bring it.
examples: I get a new book today.
Please get your coat.
She got a letter.

more.def: To receive or obtain something, or to go and bring it back.
examples: My sister got a bike for her birthday.
Can you get the scissors from the kitchen drawer?
We get snow here almost every winter.

easy.def: To become something.
examples: I get sleepy at night.
It gets cold in winter.
She got tall this year.

more.def: To change into a different condition or state.
examples: The sky gets dark when a storm is coming.
He got nervous before the spelling bee.
Ice cream gets soft if you leave it in the sun.

easy.def: A short trip for a rest.
examples: We went on a weekend getaway.
The cabin is a nice getaway.
A getaway to the beach.

more.def: A short trip, or a place you go to rest and be away from your normal life.
examples: We took a weekend getaway to the beach.
The cabin in the woods is a peaceful getaway.
A getaway to the mountains made a nice break from school.

easy.def: A funny set of clothes.
examples: He wore a silly getup.
Her getup was a clown costume.
What a getup!

more.def: An outfit of clothes, especially one that looks odd.
examples: He wore a silly getup with a big hat.
The clown's getup had huge shoes.
She showed up in a pirate getup.

easy.def: A hot spring that shoots water into the air.
examples: The geyser shot up.
A geyser is hot.
We saw a geyser.

more.def: A natural hot spring that shoots a jet of hot water and steam into the air.
examples: The geyser shot water high into the air.
Old Faithful is a famous geyser.
We waited for the geyser to erupt.
